title: Performance

# Performance characteristics

`fetch_sentinel_data` is what determines end-to-end wall time for a
typical pipeline call. It has two cost centres: network I/O to the
selected provider, and CPU-bound warp / reproject in
[`_read_band_to_grid`](https://github.com/buckai-observatory/geoai-datacubes/blob/main/geoai_datacubes/fetch/fetch_data.py).
Which one dominates depends on AOI size, band count, provider, and how
warm the STAC endpoint's cache happens to be for your bbox.

This page reports what we actually measured on two machines. It does
**not** promise the same numbers on other hardware or over other
networks; users should re-run the harness described below on their own
setup for anything load-bearing.

## Measured throughput

**Configuration:** each row is a full `fetch_sentinel_data(...)` call
returning a georeferenced multi-band GeoTIFF. AOIs are centred on
Cleveland, OH — a mixed urban / suburban / lake-shore box that
exercises multiple same-day scene mosaics in most missions. AOI sizes:
**small ≈ 25 km²**, **medium ≈ 100 km²**, **large ≈ 400 km²**. Time
ranges are one growing-season month for time-varying missions, unset
for static products (DEMs, Hansen tree cover).

Each configuration was run **n = 3** times per machine (n = 2 for the
three configurations that were mis-configured in the harness's first
laptop run — S1-RTC bands lowercased, `3DEP-seamless` vs `3DEP`,
Landsat time range too narrow — fixed and re-run for runs 2 and 3).
Wall time is reported as **min – median – max** across those runs;
output size and produced-pixel rate use the median.

*Skipped rows for missing credentials:* `Sentinel-2-L1C via sentinelhub`
and `PlanetScope via planet` — neither machine had the requisite
`SH_CLIENT_ID` / `PL_API_KEY` env vars set. The harness (see
`smoke-tests/perf_bench.py`) skips these cleanly rather than treating
them as failures.

### Unity HPC — OSU cluster, `batch` partition, 32-core Xeon node (4 requested), 16 GB, Linux, Python 3.12

| Row | Provider | AOI | n | Wall min–med–max (s) | Out (MB) | Out (Mpx) | Mpx/s |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S2-earthsearch small | `earthsearch` | 25 km² | 3 | 9.0 – 9.4 – 11.0 | 2.3 | 1.13 | 0.12 |
| S2-earthsearch medium | `earthsearch` | 100 km² | 3 | 8.6 – 9.1 – 9.2 | 8.9 | 4.53 | 0.50 |
| S2-earthsearch large | `earthsearch` | 400 km² | 3 | 8.3 – 9.5 – 10.3 | 38.9 | 20.4 | 2.14 |
| Cop-DEM medium | `earthsearch` | 100 km² | 3 | 2.6 – 3.5 – 3.6 | 0.2 | 0.10 | 0.03 |
| S1-RTC medium | `planetary_computer` | 100 km² | 3 | 7.2 – 7.4 – 7.9 | 6.3 | 1.81 | 0.24 |
| Landsat-8 medium | `planetary_computer` | 100 km² | 3 | 4.9 – 5.4 – 5.5 | 0.7 | 0.30 | 0.06 |
| NAIP small | `planetary_computer` | 25 km² | 3 | 793.8 – 806.6 – 818.7 | 303.0 | 90.5 | 0.11 |
| 3DEP small | `planetary_computer` | 25 km² | 3 | 5.5 – 5.5 – 5.6 | 0.6 | 0.23 | 0.04 |
| Hansen-GFC medium | `direct_http` | 100 km² | 3 | 9.8 – 10.2 – 13.7 | 0.8 | 0.60 | 0.06 |
| Hansen-GFC large | `direct_http` | 400 km² | 3 | 12.9 – 15.0 – 19.9 | 3.5 | 2.72 | 0.18 |

**Column notes**: `Out (MB)` is the on-disk multi-band mosaic GeoTIFF
size, not raw bytes downloaded from the source — COGs are window-read,
so upstream traffic is typically 2–10× the output. `Out (Mpx)` is
`bands × width × height` of that tiff. `Mpx/s` is the corresponding
produced-pixel rate, a scale-invariant proxy for pipeline throughput.

### Laptop ↔ Unity comparison (using medians)

| Row | Laptop | Unity | Unity speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S2 small | 11.2 s | 9.4 s | 1.2× |
| S2 medium | 14.4 s | 9.1 s | **1.6×** |
| S2 large | 9.7 s | 9.5 s | ~1.0× |
| Cop-DEM | 3.8 s | 3.5 s | 1.1× |
| S1-RTC | 8.8 s | 7.4 s | 1.2× |
| Landsat-8 | 8.7 s | 5.4 s | **1.6×** |
| NAIP | 724 s | 807 s | **0.9× (laptop faster)** |
| 3DEP | 7.7 s | 5.5 s | 1.4× |
| Hansen medium | 20.8 s | 10.2 s | **2.0×** |
| Hansen large | 25.1 s | 15.0 s | **1.7×** |

## What dominates runtime

Three patterns fall out of the numbers above:

1. **Small AOIs are setup-bound, not bandwidth-bound.** A 25 km² S2
   fetch spends most of its wall time on STAC search, per-band grid
   setup, and rasterio's session-open overhead — the actual asset
   download for ~1 M pixels @ 10 m is trivial. This is why the two
   machines are nearly tied for the 25 km² rows: institutional
   bandwidth doesn't help when nothing is downloading yet.

2. **Larger AOIs and `direct_http` benefit most from good bandwidth.**
   Hansen GFC (Google Cloud Storage) shows a 2× speedup on Unity
   because a bigger fraction of wall time is actual bytes flowing.
   Sentinel-2 large also amortises the fixed setup cost well.

3. **`planetary_computer` NAIP is the exception.** NAIP is served
   through a bursty tile pipeline whose upstream throughput is
   independent of the client's bandwidth to Azure. Neither cellular
   nor Unity moves the needle much — both take ~12 minutes for
   ~90 Mpx. If NAIP throughput is a bottleneck for your workflow,
   the win comes from batching (multiple AOIs in parallel via
   [`fetch/parallel_fetch.py`](https://github.com/buckai-observatory/geoai-datacubes/blob/main/geoai_datacubes/fetch/parallel_fetch.py))
   rather than from faster interconnect.

An anomaly worth noting: **S2 large ran consistently faster than S2
medium on laptop** (medians 9.7 s vs 14.4 s, three runs each, no
overlap). This isn't noise — it's because the "large" bbox happens to
hit a cleaner 2-scene mosaic than the "medium", which the greedy
scene-selection heuristic pays for slightly. It's a quirk of the AOI
choice, not a pipeline pathology.

## Levers users have

The knobs that actually move the wall time, in rough order of impact:

1. **`resolution`** — quadratic. Doubling it (10 m → 20 m) quarters
   the pixel count and roughly quarters both the fetch (fewer COG
   tiles/windows read) and the reproject stage. For sanity-checking a
   pipeline before committing to a full 10 m run, 30–60 m often
   suffices.

2. **`bands`** — linear. Passing an explicit `bands=["B04","B08"]`
   instead of `bands=None` (which expands to the mission's
   `default_bands + extra_bands` — 5 bands for S2, up to 8 for
   Sentinel-3, etc.) proportionally reduces fetch and reproject time.

3. **AOI size** — roughly linear in area for large AOIs, sub-linear
   for small ones (setup dominates).

4. **Provider selection** — for missions available on multiple
   providers (see [`docs/providers.md`](providers.md)), `earthsearch`
   is typically the fastest cold-cache option for Sentinel-2 (AWS
   Open Data), while `planetary_computer` is best for Sentinel-1 RTC
   (analysis-ready) and Landsat C2 L2 (free, not requester-pays).
   `sentinelhub` and `planet` have request latency dominated by
   OAuth / order-processing steps and are best reserved for cases
   where their unique offerings (S3-OLCI, PlanetScope daily) actually
   matter.

5. **Concurrency** — for the multi-AOI case, `parallel_fetch.py`
   wraps a `ThreadPoolExecutor` around per-AOI calls. Provider
   rate-limits (see [`docs/providers.md`](providers.md)) are the
   ceiling here.

## Reproducing these numbers

The benchmark harness lives at
[`smoke-tests/perf_bench.py`](https://github.com/buckai-observatory/geoai-datacubes/blob/main/smoke-tests/perf_bench.py).
Its `--configs all` preset runs the 12 rows above; `--configs credfree`
skips the two OAuth-gated ones. Each row's raw JSON log lands in
`smoke-tests/perf_logs/` (gitignored — outputs stay local).

Laptop run:
```{.bash}
python smoke-tests/perf_bench.py --configs all --label laptop
```

SLURM (Unity or similar):
```{.bash}
sbatch --export=ALL,ENV_NAME=<your-env>,LABEL=hpc \
       smoke-tests/perf_bench.slurm
```

Once you have JSON logs from one or more runs on one or more machines,
aggregate them into a min-med-max table with
[`smoke-tests/perf_bench_agg.py`](https://github.com/buckai-observatory/geoai-datacubes/blob/main/smoke-tests/perf_bench_agg.py):

```{.bash}
python smoke-tests/perf_bench_agg.py \
    --machine laptop \
    --machine hpc
```

The aggregator collapses per-run suffixes (`laptop-run2`,
`laptop-run3`, …) into a single `laptop` column, so repeat runs stack
cleanly.

## Honest caveats

- **These are single-machine measurements**, not benchmarks in a
  formal sense. n = 3 per row is enough to expose the ~15–30 %
  run-to-run variance visible in the tables above (a real signal —
  cellular provider bandwidth fluctuates; STAC endpoint caches warm
  and cool), but not enough for confidence intervals on tail latency.
- **Provider behaviour changes.** Planetary Computer's SAS-signed
  Azure endpoints have re-tiered several times since 2023;
  earthsearch has swapped between requester-pays and open buckets for
  different S2 collections; the ETH canopy-height mirror serving Lang
  2023 is a single university web server whose availability varies.
  Numbers here reflect August–September 2026.
- **We don't measure the ML surfaces.** `LazyTileDataset`,
  `geotiff_to_zarr`, and the tile-based fusion pipeline all have
  their own performance characteristics that aren't covered here.
  Add them to the harness if that's your bottleneck.

For provider-by-provider capability trade-offs and rate-limit
guidance, see [`docs/providers.md`](providers.md). For the pipeline
shape being measured, see [`docs/architecture.qmd`](architecture.qmd).
